item.description: ### Fixed - **Jump-to-terminal works again on macOS 26.** macOS 26 stopped letting Perch read another process's environment, which is where a session's terminal and pane used to come from. Every Amp session and every Antigravity session lost its terminal, and a click fell back to opening the folder. Perch now finds the terminal from the process tree instead, and for iTerm2 finds the exact pane from the session's tty. Warp's exact pane cannot be recovered this way; Warp sessions raise the app. - **The phone can no longer type into a shell.** `claude -p`, `codex e`, `codex review`, `cursor-agent -fp` and `devin -cp` are print modes with no prompt: text sent to their pane waits in the terminal and the shell runs it when they exit. Claude had no check at all, Codex missed the alias, and the others missed clustered flags. All are refused now, and so is an agent whose command line Perch cannot read. - **Replying from a Mac notification checks the agent is still there.** A reply left in Notification Center after the agent had exited was typed into whatever that terminal was showing — a shell, or a stranger's tab. Perch now re-checks the agent immediately before typing, and refuses under Zellij, where the reply would land in whichever pane happened to be focused. - **A lapsed Pro key stays lapsed offline.** When the licence server could not be reached, every key Perch held was treated as valid, with no expiry, so a revoked or expired Pro key came back on any network blip. Each key now remembers its own last answer, and an outage honours only that. - **Perch never overwrites your hooks.** A `hooks` block in `~/.claude/settings.json` or `~/.codex/hooks.json` with a shape Perch does not recognise used to be replaced wholesale with Perch's own entries. Perch now leaves the file alone and says why. - **Usage meters tell the truth more often.** Codex's context percentage no longer double-counts cached tokens. Amp's cycle no longer shows an invented 0% "reset" in the hours between midnight and the real renewal. An idle session replaying an old reading can no longer keep a fresher one out, and a real re-baseline from a live session takes effect at once. A malformed usage response can no longer crash the low-usage warning. - **Codex sessions stop flickering to idle mid-turn.** A scan that read no turn boundary, or read the previous turn's, could mark a running session idle for a tick — and hide it under "hide idle". Only a boundary written after the current turn began can do that now. - **Cursor sessions stop firing "finished" mid-turn.** A transcript read that landed on a half-written character counted as an empty transcript. - **Stats no longer count Codex subagents as sessions.** - **Phone and watch approvals are honest.** The Live Activity countdown is now the provider's real window (five minutes for OpenCode; none for Amp and Antigravity, which never time out). Needs companion app 1.0.6 build 55 or later for the rest: the watch no longer offers Allow/Deny for an agent question, and a tap on an unreachable Mac no longer closes the sheet as if it had been heard.
